title: Equal hourly normal laws and correlations gave daily flood risks of 7.21% and 21.08% in a 24-hour test
abstract: We test whether exact hourly normal distributions and residual correlations determine daily flood risk. A stationary sign chain with a common half-normal magnitude and a Gaussian AR(1) model have identical hourly laws and covariance at every lag. With 24 hours, lag-one correlation 0.95 and 5% hourly risk, daily risk is 7.21% and 21.08%. A smooth model with the same inputs has risk bounded between 6.36% and 8.14%. These values imply a numerical lower bound of 6.47 percentage points on the worst absolute error of any method that uses only the shared inputs. A separate analytic two-hour bound proves non-identification without the full Gaussian integration. We supply an exact finite-sum calculator for positive unequal thresholds, a Gaussian Markov recursion, 48 synthetic cases and independent simulation. The general insufficiency of correlation is established prior knowledge; this study gives a quantitative daily flood stress test. No model is fitted to ocean data. Synthetic tides, a non-ergodic process extension and numerical quadrature limit the scope. The result does not explain issued NOAA forecast errors or give an operational correction.

display.caption: Two models have identical hourly laws and full covariance, but different daily flood risk. All inputs are synthetic.
